hero.headline: Tomasz Kowalski – a lawyer who knows both sides of the process
hero.subheadline: For 5 years I served as a prosecutor at the Regional Prosecutor's Office in Warsaw, and for over 15 years I have been running my own law practice. I protect the freedom, assets, and reputation of entrepreneurs and individuals alike. This unique experience on both sides of the barricade enables me to build effective defence strategies grounded in a thorough understanding of prosecutorial mechanisms. I have also delivered presentations at over 30 legal conferences.

bio.name: Tomasz Kowalski, Esq.
bio.role: Advocate / Legal counsel specialising in criminal and white-collar criminal law
bio.imageAlt: Lawyer Tomasz Kowalski – Law Office Warsaw
bio.summary: I am an advocate admitted to the roll of the Warsaw District Bar Council. I specialise in defence in criminal and white-collar criminal cases, with a particular focus on protecting entrepreneurs and board members. My mission is to ensure that every client receives diligent, committed, and effective defence – regardless of the gravity of the charges.

education.institution: University of Warsaw, Faculty of Law and Administration

education.degree: Postgraduate studies in financial and tax law

items.institution: Law Office of Tomasz Kowalski, Esq., Warsaw
items.description: Running an individual advocacy practice specialising in criminal and white-collar criminal law. Representing clients before prosecutors' offices and courts of all instances. Providing legal services to enterprises in the financial, construction, trade, and technology sectors. Since 2015, I have exclusively handled criminal and white-collar criminal cases.

Work in the Investigative Department and the Organised Crime Department. Conducting investigations into economic, financial, and property offences. Experience in preparing indictments and representing the public prosecutor before courts.

items.institution: University of Warsaw, Faculty of Law and Administration
items.description: Teaching criminal procedure and white-collar criminal law to law students. Delivering conference lectures on the defence of board members in criminal proceedings.

items.title: Certified specialist in white-collar criminal law
items.description: Certification issued by the Polish Bar Association upon passing the specialisation examination. Confirmation of competencies in defence in cases concerning economic, fiscal, and corruption offences.

items.title: Member of an international legal organisation
items.description: Member of the International Association of Defence Lawyers (IADL). Cooperation with law firms from the United Kingdom, Germany, the United States, and Switzerland in cross-border cases.

items.title: Speaker at legal conferences
items.description: Presentations as a speaker at over 30 conferences and training sessions on white-collar criminal law, compliance, and board member protection. Publications in legal journals: "Palestra", "Criminal Law Review", "Legal Monitor".

items.title: Industry recommendations
items.description: Regularly recommended in Legal500 EMEA and Chambers Europe legal directories in the Crime: White-Collar Crime category. Confirmation of a position among the leading criminal defence advocates in Poland.

items.title: Absolute loyalty to the client
items.description: Every client receives my full dedication. I do not accept cases in which I cannot commit 100%. Each case is a priority – regardless of its gravity.

items.title: Honest assessment of prospects
items.description: I do not promise unrealistic outcomes. At the initial consultation I assess the situation honestly, identifying both the strengths and weaknesses of the case. The client makes decisions based on facts, not promises.

items.title: Constant availability
items.description: Criminal cases do not wait until morning. Clients have my direct phone number and can reach me in urgent situations. I respond to messages within a few hours.

items.title: Continuous professional development
items.description: Criminal law evolves – case law, statutes, and interpretations change. I regularly attend training sessions, read legal literature, and share knowledge as a lecturer. This enables me to provide defence at the highest current standard.

items.title: Criminal liability of board members of commercial companies – current issues and case law
items.description: Analysis of the latest Supreme Court case law concerning the limits of criminal liability of board members for acts undertaken on behalf of the company.

items.title: Voluntary submission to a penalty in white-collar criminal cases – when is it worth agreeing?
items.description: Practical analysis of the benefits and risks associated with voluntary submission to a penalty in cases of economic fraud and mismanagement.

items.title: The right to defence at the stage of detention and search – a review of ECtHR case law
items.description: Comprehensive overview of European Court of Human Rights standards concerning the rights of a detainee, including the right to contact a lawyer.

items.question: Do you accept cases from other cities?
items.answer: Yes. My office is based in Warsaw, but I handle cases throughout the entire country. In white-collar criminal cases I frequently appear before prosecutors' offices and courts in Kraków, Wrocław, Poznań, Gdańsk, and Łódź. Travel arrangements are agreed on a case-by-case basis.

items.question: Do you collaborate with other lawyers?
items.answer: In cases requiring broader support, I cooperate with affiliated law firms specialising in civil, tax, and administrative law. The client always has one lead defence counsel – me – but benefits from a breadth of competencies.

items.question: Do you handle cases involving minors?
items.answer: Yes. I represent minors in proceedings before family courts and in criminal cases where the accused or suspect is under 18 years of age. In such cases I pay particular attention to protecting the privacy and rights of the minor.

items.question: Do you give media interviews?
items.answer: I do not comment on pending cases in the media. Client privacy is my priority. I appear in the media exclusively as a commentator on general legal issues – never in the context of specific proceedings in which I represent a client.
